request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in, and all 4 Playwright tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- **New `Rollup` service** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`): it works out each person's claimed and due-total and the sheet's two totals on the server. It uses the same rules as the screen: only OPEN and SETTLED claims count, settled or stated figures stay fixed, a due-total is n/a when the grade has no rate today and no claim keeps a figure, and the sheet's due-total skips n/a.
- **Before each change:** I added a `snapshot` step right after `validate` in the 8 endpoints that change data: add person, edit person, add claim, edit claim, claim status, statement, set rate and set today. It records the figures before anything is written.
- **After each change:** each endpoint's existing audit or save step calls `rollup.recordChanges(...)` after writing its own audit line. That compares before and after and writes:
  - a `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved (or who is new), in the order people were added;
  - a `TOTALS` line if either sheet total moved.
- **Refused changes:** these lines are only written when the change is committed, like the existing audit lines, so a refused change writes none.
- **Setting today:** `ValidateToday` now also passes the request on, so the today change knows who made it. It gets no audit line of its own, only rollup lines when figures move.

**One difference from the request:** the request words the line as `ROLLUP name=<name> …`, but the test expects `ROLLUP sheet=<id> by=<user> person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…`. The `TOTALS` line likewise starts with `sheet=` and `by=`. I followed the test.

No front-end or database changes were needed.
